title: A Medium-Throughput Single Cell CRISPR-Cas9 Assay to Assess Gene Essentiality
author: Grassian, Scales, et al.
materials: The region around the Cas9 cut site targeted by the sgRNA in either EZH2 or the ROSA26 locus was amplified by PCR using primers of the same sequence as for the digest analysis, with the forward primer tagged with FAM. Resultant PCR products were purified using Diffinity RapidTips (Sigma) and diluted 1:50 in H2O. Capillary electrophoresis was performed on the samples (Source Biosciences) using Liz-600 size standards; fragment length was determined using Genemapper5 software (Applied Biosystems).

steps.title: Amplify target region for restriction digest
steps.instruction: Perform PCR on the region surrounding the Cas9 cut site using the primers forward AGGCAAACCCTGAAGAACTG and reverse ATGGCTCTCTTGGCAAAAAT.

steps.title: Digest PCR product with FauI
steps.instruction: Incubate the PCR amplicon with the restriction enzyme FauI, which directly overlaps the Cas9 cut site for the EZH2‑targeting sgRNA.

steps.title: Run agarose gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Separate the FauI‑digested PCR products on an agarose gel and visualize the bands.

steps.title: Assess genotype of FauI site
steps.instruction: Determine the genotype (heterozygous disrupted, homozygous disrupted, or homozygous un‑disrupted) based on the presence or absence of the FauI cut site in the gel image.

steps.title: Amplify region for fragment length analysis
steps.instruction: Perform PCR on the Cas9 cut‑site region (EZH2 or ROSA26) using the same primer sequences as above, but with the forward primer labeled with FAM.

steps.title: Purify and dilute PCR products
steps.instruction: Purify the FAM‑labeled PCR products with Diffinity RapidTips (Sigma) and dilute the eluate 1:50 in H₂O.

steps.title: Capillary electrophoresis and fragment sizing
steps.instruction: Run the diluted samples on a capillary electrophoresis system (Source Biosciences) using Liz‑600 size standards; analyze fragment lengths with Genemapper 5 software (Applied Biosystems).
